title: P02 follow-up: triple decoupled weight decay on the Muon matrices (MUON_WD 0.01 -> 0.03) on the bs-128 incumbent
description: P02 follow-up (Muon weight-decay convention, cf. Moonlight): the only edit multiplies the Muon group's decoupled weight decay by 3 (MUON_WD 0.01 -> 0.03; per-step shrinkage 1e-4 -> 3e-4 at peak LR), leaving the AdamW group, LRs, batch and schedule identical to incumbent 066-claude. Currently the Muon decay time constant (~10k steps) exceeds the ~4760-step run, so hidden weights are growth-dominated and accumulate random-walk noise from small-batch Muon steps; stronger decay should hand RL smaller, cleaner weights that its fixed AdamW (lr 3e-4) can move relatively further.
hypothesis: Under Muon each step adds an update of fixed spectral size, so weight norms grow with step count; at bs 128 (4760 steps) the noise component of that growth is not removed by the current decay (cumulative factor 0.77). Tripling decay (cumulative factor ~0.46, time constant ~3.3k steps) keeps directions the gradient consistently needs (equilibrium spectral scale ~1/wd = 33, far above what attention sharpness needs) while shrinking accumulated noise. Smaller, less noisy pretrained weights should (a) generalize slightly better past 6-line proofs and (b) be more plastic under the frozen RL AdamW, whose relative step size scales as lr/||W||, so expert iteration extends to 7+ line proofs faster. Consistent with 066 (2x steps, hence 2x cumulative decay, +23 with unchanged val loss) and 055 (1.5x Muon LR at fixed per-step decay, larger weights, -35).
expected_delta: -40 to +25 theorems at >=7 (central guess -3); pretraining val loss within +-0.004 of 066's 0.0915-0.0956, possibly a smaller train/val gap; round-1 RL sample accuracy >= 066's (0.053/0.061/0.071) on at least two seeds if the plasticity mechanism holds

arch.change: none versus 066-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 066-claude except Muon weight decay)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: CHANGED: MUON_WD = 3 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.03, so Muon lr*0.03 is three times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 per-step shrinkage at every schedule fraction (peak 3e-4 per step instead of 1e-4). Applies to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight. AdamW group decay (wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3) is unchanged. Summed over ~4760 steps (mean schedule factor ~0.55) the cumulative multiplicative decay factor is ~exp(-0.79)=0.46 instead of ~exp(-0.26)=0.77.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 066-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 066-claude.
